items.title: Кин-дза-дза!
verified_facts: Both institutions credit Georgiy Daneliya as director and label the film 1986.
Both credit Daneliya and Revaz Gabriadze for the screenplay; Pavel Lebeshev for cinematography; Kancheli for music.
The studio synopsis describes two Earth travellers encountering unfamiliar customs; the museum characterizes the film as satire.
editorial_limits: The studio synopsis calls the title a planet name. Do not reproduce that geographic claim without separate scene-level verification; neither reviewed page resolves the fictional geography.
Museum production anecdotes, awards and quotations are outside this proposed article scope. Do not copy them.
Do not conflate Revaz Gabriadze (screenplay) with Levan Gabriadze (cast).
items.proposed_exercise: An explicitly interpretive comparison of unfamiliar customs with familiar social rules; no assertion of measured difficulty.

items.title: Человек с бульвара Капуцинов
verified_facts: Studio card labels the film 1987 and credits Alla Surikova as director, Eduard Akopov for screenplay and Gennady Gladkov for music.
Its synopsis places Johnny Fest in a cowboy town, exhibiting cinema in a saloon; Diana and the rival exhibitor Second are named.
Andrei Mironov, Nikolai Karachentsov and Alexandra Yakovleva appear in the cast list; this page does not explicitly bind each actor to a role.
editorial_limits: One producing-studio source, not independently corroborated.
Keep the 1987 work distinct from the similarly titled later film; this page alone is not evidence about that other work.
Do not infer actor-role bindings, shooting anecdotes, prizes or lyrics from the cast list.
items.proposed_exercise: Compare how two exhibitors influence the same audience; label the learning prompt as interpretation.

items.title: Жестокий романс
verified_facts: Studio card labels the film 1984 and credits Eldar Ryazanov as director and screenwriter.
The synopsis identifies an adaptation based on Alexander Ostrovsky's play Without a Dowry (Bespridannitsa).
Andrei Petrov is credited for music and Vadim Alisov for cinematography. Larisa Guzeeva and Nikita Mikhalkov are in the cast list.
editorial_limits: One producing-studio source, not independently corroborated.
Do not equate play authorship with screen direction or claim a literal adaptation.
The page does not prove individual singing/voice credits, actor-role bindings, precise production history or critical consensus.
items.proposed_exercise: Separate the author of the play from the screenwriter and director; discuss the difference between affection and calculation as a reading prompt.

items.title: Мимино
verified_facts: Studio card labels the film 1977 and credits Georgiy Daneliya as director.
The screenplay credits name Daneliya, Viktoriya Tokareva and Revaz Gabriadze; music credit is Kancheli.
The synopsis names Valiko Mizandari, nicknamed Mimino, a helicopter pilot travelling to Moscow in pursuit of larger-scale aviation.
The cast includes Vakhtang Kikabidze and Frunzik Mkrtchyan.
editorial_limits: One producing-studio source, not independently corroborated.
Do not present the success-versus-belonging interpretation as a documented statement of the director's intention.
Do not infer every actor-role binding, musical performance credit or production anecdote from the cast list.
items.proposed_exercise: Use the synopsis to compare achieving a professional goal with a feeling of belonging; leave the response open rather than supplying an invented objective answer.

source_limit: Four studio cards plus one museum page; only item011 has two institutionally distinct sources. Links are evidence, not media reuse permission.
